title: The canonical coefficient-unit direct-image arrow

source.place: paragraph (1), applying coefficient extension to the positive section class; trace proof paragraph (1), its adjunction

statement: Let A and B be abelian categories with fixed compatible derived-category universes, and F:A to B an additive functor with specified DiagonalRightDerived D. For an object M of A [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-models], define singlePushComparison D M from single(F M) to D.R(single M) by the inverse single-complex comparison followed by D.eta. It is natural in M. For an exact square with its full universal-unit normalization [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-models], its evaluation on a single object is the ordinary comparison followed by singlePushComparison. For a condensed commutative coefficient ring Lambda and Y [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-category], coefficientOrdinaryUnit is the ordinary pullback-adjoint of the inverse monoidal unit isomorphism, with underlying map condensedPushforwardHom; coefficientUnitPush is single of this ordinary pullback-adjoint of the inverse monoidal unit isomorphism, followed by this comparison for the regular module on P=ProjectiveLine Y. finiteUnitAdjunct is the canonical finite derived adjunct of geoP1UnitPullback, with fixed finite-unit endpoints; finiteAdjunct is the canonical adjunct of any local finite arrow, again with fixed source and target; composing the unit adjunct with a pushed arrow computes finiteAdjunct by adjunction naturality. These are explicit constructions, without arbitrary choices.

proof.text: Construct the single-object comparison by the inverse degree-zero comparison and the specified universal derived unit. Naturality follows from naturality of these two maps. Evaluate the full exact-square normalization on a single complex; naturality and a degreewise check cancel all single-complex comparisons. Define coefficientUnitPush by composing this comparison with the ordinary adjoint of the inverse monoidal-unit isomorphism.
